What it would do differently

The leads the player wrote, each with where it happened and what would settle it. An ask is a link into the replay above.

  1. How many down staircases does a level really have, and where?

    Source answer: exactly one (gen-cave.c:1583), placed uniformly at random among squares with 3 adjacent walls (gen-util.c:620 + cave_find_get_grid's randint0 over the whole level).

    To confirm empirically: a run that buys a Magic Mapping scroll, reads it on depth 1, and reports whether one > appears in the 22×40 window.

  2. Does the M whole-level map show the whole level or only the remembered part?

    On depth 1 it showed the eastern third; on depth 2 it showed a 7×3 blob while the main map had drawn a 13-wide room.

    To settle it: map a level, then compare the M view's extent with the number of squares the main map has ever drawn.

  3. What is the true relationship between > on the map and the staircase?

    Evidence: the > was on the depth-1 map at ask 160 but the M view at ask 156 did not show it, and the M view at ask 260 did not show depth 2's (absent) one.

    To settle: a run that walks over a staircase, then presses M, and says whether the > appears in the remembered map.

    ask 160, 156, 260 · turn 7,433-9,002

  4. How common is a Deep Descent scroll on depth 2, and where?

    It is alloc:20:1 to 100 from depth 1 (object.txt), and I did not find one in 250 asks.

    To settle: read the allocation code in obj-make.c for whether alloc_min/alloc_max or level governs depth, and run several depth-2 levels looking for ? on the floor.

  5. What is the experience economy on depth 2, measured against a druid's spell-point cost?

    Level 3 needs 25 units for a High-Elf; Grip alone was worth 30.

    To settle: a table of experience: per depth-2 monster against the turns a CL3 druid must spend resting to pay for one Stinking Cloud (about 43).

  6. Is a Druid viable in this game at all?

    Hit die 2 plus CON, 13 HP at CL1, a 1d3+1 whip, a spellbook whose spells cost 43 turns of rest each, and no teleport spell ever. I got to CL4 and depth 2 alive and killed a unique with oil.

    To settle: a druid run that reaches CL5 and casts Stinking Cloud twice in a row — if the spell still cannot keep up with the mana, the class's answer is oil and the scroll.

  7. Is the town worth returning to?

    The Alchemist restocks daily and the stock rotates; a cutpurse took gold and an oil flask there.

    To settle: a run that returns to town on several different days and records the Alchemist's and Black Market's stock each time, and whether the thieves take more when you are loaded.

- Giant black ant: 11 hp, AC 24, 1d4 bite, exp 8 (monster.txt) - and it is ASLEEP ('unhurt, asleep'). - THROW MISSED the sleeping ant at distance 2 (ask 201: 'The giant black ant is targeted... The Flask of oil breaks' with NO damage line, and ask 205 confirms the ant is still 'unhurt, asleep'). Source reading (vendor/angband/src/player-attack.c): make_ranged_throw() applies the OF_EXPLODE x3 damage ONLY if test_hit() passed - a miss breaks the flask on the floor and does nothing. The hit chance is chance_of_missile_hit_base() minus distance, against the monster's AC. The ant's AC 24 (monster.txt) is brutal: hit_chance() needs to_hit >= ac*2/3 = 16 to have any chance above the flat 12% always-hit, so at range you are mostly rolling the 12%. (ask 205)

Lesser Charms is a nature book with 6 spells. The CL2 spell Remove Hunger is worth little (food is not a time pressure here - digestion is 1 unit per 100 turns, per my inherited note), so Stinking Cloud at CL3 is the prize, if the game lets me study a spell above my level. (ask 210)
- Studied Remove Hunger at ask 217: 'You have learned the verse of Remove Hunger.' and NXT stayed at 7 - so STUDYING a spell costs no experience; the exp field in class.txt (Detect Life 2, Fox Form 10, Remove Hunger 2) is the FIRST CAST cost, not the learning cost. Also confirmed the game REFUSES to study a spell above your class level: at CL2 pressing 'd' (Stinking Cloud, CL3) in the Study prompt did nothing and left the prompt up. So a druid must reach CL3 before Stinking Cloud can be learned, and 'Study (1)' means one verse per character level. (ask 217)
- KEY ERROR OF MINE, worth recording so no next run repeats it: after pressing 'l' (look) the look mode STAYS ACTIVE and swallows the next command's first key. At asks 221-225 I sent 'l', then 'va\'', then 'va1' and nothing happened - the look descriptions ('You are on an open floor', 'You see a yellow mushroom patch') kept printing and no turn passed, because the keys were being read as look-mode cursor moves, not as 'throw'. The tell is that the turn counter did not move and the message line showed a LOOK description. Press '\e' to leave look mode before any other command. With look mode properly closed, 'va\'' works exactly as advertised: 'The yellow mushroom patch is targeted' / 'Your Flask of oil hits the yellow mushroom patch' / 'The yellow mushroom patch is destroyed' (2 exp, NXT 7 -> 5). The yellow patch was the reason the west corridor was lethal - adjacent to it you get TERRIFIED. (ask 229)
- TWO OIL THROWS AT THE SMALL KOBOLD BOTH MISSED (asks 235, 236) and it hit me for 2 (HP 20/22). Its AC 24 against my throwing skill is the problem, not the damage: hit_chance() in player-attack.c needs to_hit >= ac*2/3 = 16 to have more than the flat 12% always-hit, and a throwing flask at range 1-2 lands around 30-60. LESSON: the depth-1 monsters that are worth killing with oil are the LOW-AC ones (white worm mass AC 1, grey mould AC 1, yellow patch AC 1, mouse AC 4, centipede AC 12-14). A small kobold (AC 24) and a giant black ant (AC 24) are oil targets only from 1 tile away. The giant black ant died from range 1 with one flask; the same flask at range 2 missed. (ask 237)
- Detect Life at ask 238 said 'You sense life!' and set MFLAG_MARK+MFLAG_SHOW on every living, non-camouflaged monster within 22 rows x 40 columns (vendor/angband/src/effect-handler-general.c detect_monsters). The map then shows them even outside the light radius - but the text dump I get does not show the blinking MARK highlight, only the SHOW part, so the detection is of limited use to me as a player: I see 'You sense life!' and then the map may or may not have gained glyphs outside my light. A plain-text player cannot use Detect Life the way the manual implies. Small kobold killed at ask 240 (2 oil flasks, both at range 1), NXT 5 -> 3, so 3 more units for CL3 and Stinking Cloud. (ask 240)
- GLYPH TABLE now decoded from vendor/angband/lib/gamedata/terrain.txt (each 'graphics:<char>:<colour>' line): space=unknown grid, .=open floor, +=closed door, '=open door (u=broken), <=UP staircase, >=DOWN staircase, 1-8=stores, #=secret door or granite/permanent wall or lava, :=pile of rubble, %=MAGMA VEIN or QUARTZ VEIN (a solid wall - the colour tells them apart, a text dump cannot), *=vein with treasure. So the corridor I am in is a vein-walled passage: the '%' above and below me are walls, not floor, and the fact that they are drawn '%' and not '#' only tells me they are rock veins. There is no '>' anywhere on the map of depth 2 yet. (ask 243)
- THE '[' COMMAND IS THE BEST ONE-ASK SCAN IN THE GAME: it prints 'You can see N monsters:' with the glyph, the COUNT, the name and the exact relative position of each - e.g. 'c   1 giant yellow centipede    2 S 0 W' (ask 245). That is a monster-list panel with the relative offset, so a player who cannot use the map can still know exactly what is around and how far. It even offers 'Press x to turn ON sort by exp'. Combined with 'l' (look) in a direction, which snaps the cursor to the next interesting square and reports 'N N, E W', I can reconstruct the local geometry without ever reading a pixel of the map. (ask 245)
- QUAFF SEQUENCE that works in one ask: 'q' then 'd' (the quaff prompt prints 'Quaff which potion? (Inven: d-d)' and the pack letter selects it). 'qdq' does NOT work - the third key is read as the Drop option of the item command menu, and the game then asks 'Drop which item?'. Also 'q d ' opens the item-command menu instead of the quaff prompt; pressing 'q' there quaffs. So: q, d. (ask 253)
- M (whole-level map) on depth 2 at ask 260 shows ONLY the region I have seen - a blob about 18 map columns wide around me - drawn at a scale that differs from the main map, so I still cannot read absolute level coordinates out of it. The main map's window also scrolls, so my absolute position is not recoverable from a single screen either. PRACTICAL CONCLUSION for the report: the level is 198x66 (constants.txt dungeon-wid/dungeon-hgt) and the map window is 36x22, so a level is about five screens wide and three tall; locating a staircase by reading maps is hopeless for a text player, and the only tool that works is the game's own pathfinder (lxg) plus scanning every map for a '>' glyph. (ask 260)
- Found and picked up an UNIDENTIFIED scroll on depth 2 (ask 273), title 'imusto que', dropped by a small kobold at 100 feet. Deep Descent has level:10 and alloc:20:1 to 100 in object.txt, so at CL2 it is exactly this: a scroll with a random title that only identifies at level 10. Reading it at CL2 is what the knowledge in NOTES.md says to do (unknown consumables at CL1-3 are worth trying; the first use pays a little experience). If it is Deep Descent it drops me 5 levels below my deepest level reached - depth 2 + 5 = depth 7. Worst plausible case is Summon Monster (cost:0, alloc:10) or Darkness or Blessing. Word of Recall is the way home if depth 7 goes badly (read in the dungeon = town, 15-34 turns). (ask 274)
- The unidentified scroll on depth 2 turned out to be a Scroll of LIGHT, not Deep Descent: 'You are surrounded by a white light' then 'You have no more Scrolls of Light (g)'. So it identified at first use and cost no experience (NXT stayed at 2) - Light's exp field in class.txt/object.txt is small. Harmless, and now known. What I can say about the DROP: it was dropped by a small kobold at 100 feet (level 2), so a depth-2 kobold carried a Scroll of Light - the monster drop table is a real source of consumables, and killing a monster is a way to GET a scroll rather than hoping to find one on the floor. (ask 277)
- DECISIVE TEST of the manual's 'l>g' recipe: in look mode press '>' and the cursor jumps to the nearest KNOWN down staircase (vendor/angband/src/ui-target.c, path_nearest_known with square_isdownstairs). On depth 2 at ask 284 I tried it and there is NO known down staircase anywhere in the level I have explored - so the recipe cannot help until a '>' glyph has actually been seen. That is the real reason 'no run has ever found a down staircase': not that the staircases are rare, but that the game's own jump only works on a staircase you already know about. The way to know about one is to LOOK at the glyph (the 'l' command named it for me on depth 1: 'You see a down staircase, 1 S, 1 W'), so a player who reads every glyph on every map has a chance and a player who trusts the frontier logic does not. (ask 284)
- SOURCE ANSWER to the repo's standing question 'is the down staircase findable at all': NO SPATIAL RULE EXISTS. gen-cave.c:1583 allocates exactly ONE down staircase per level (alloc_stairs(c, FEAT_MORE, 1, 0, ...)), gen-util.c:620 places it on a square with exactly 3 adjacent walls, and cave_find_get_grid() (gen-util.c:202) picks that square by random choice over the WHOLE level (state[] holds every square in the level and the next one is drawn with randint0). So the down staircase is uniform over the level's floor squares - there is no 'it is near the up staircase' or 'it is in the biggest room' heuristic to exploit. The level is 198x66 with up to 50 rooms (dungeon_profile.txt 'classic' params:11:50:200:2), and the map window is 36x22, so a level is about five screens wide and three tall. Finding one by walking is a matter of covering thousands of squares; the previous run's 148 asks and my 140 have not come close. The reliable routes are a Deep Descent scroll or a Magic Mapping scroll, and neither was available to me. (ask 289)
- ENDGAME NOTE for the report: with one down staircase placed uniformly at random on a 198x66 level and a 36x22 map window, and no detection tool in the pack (no Magic Mapping, no Find Stairs spell for a Druid), the probability of finding it by walking in the remaining budget is small. I spent my last asks walking the corridor south of the big room, which is the region the frontier logic kept pointing at, and scanning every map I have drawn for a '>' glyph with a script over the screen files - the only real one was the depth-1 staircase at asks 160-162. Depth 2's down staircase was never seen. (ask 300)
- LEVEL 3 at ask 306 (from the sleeping giant green frog: 9 hp, AC 9, exp 6, killed with one flask of oil at range 1 - a much better oil target than anything else on this level). HP 22/26, SP 3/5, 'Study (1)' is back, and NXT 25 means CL4 is 25 experience units away. Grip, Farmer Maggot's Dog (the DL2 unique: 25 hp, AC 36, 1d4, speed 120 = +10 speed, exp 30) is 2 tiles south of me and AWAKE, so I am not going to fight it - but its 30 experience units are what CL4 wants. (ask 306)
- STINKING CLOUD SOURCE READING (effect-handler-attack.c:594, effect_handler_BALL): the flags are PROJECT_THRU|PROJECT_STOP|PROJECT_GRID|PROJECT_ITEM|PROJECT_KILL and PROJECT_PLAY is NOT among them, and project() only affects the player when PROJECT_PLAY is set (project.c:519 and :996). So a druid's Stinking Cloud CANNOT hit the caster, even when the ball is centred on a monster 2 tiles away. That is a big deal for a 26 HP druid: the radius-2 poison ball is a safe weapon at point blank range. Damage = PLAYER_LEVEL/2 + 10 = 11 poison at CL3, halved with distance from the centre. (ask 310)
- GRIP (Fang and Grip, the DL2 uniques) against a CL3 druid, measured: 25 hp, AC 36, bite 1d4, speed 120, exp 30. Stinking Cloud hit it ('yelps in pain', health bar [******----], about 55%) and cost me 12 experience on the first cast. A flask of oil at point blank MISSED - AC 36 means the throw hit chance is hopeless, the same lesson as the small kobold and the giant black ant but worse. It bit me for 5 and chased me north, so my HP is 11/26 and I have 1 SP of the 2 a cast needs. The spell is the only weapon that can hurt it, and I cannot pay for it while it is on me. (ask 318)
- THE FIGHT WITH GRIP, measured: it bites for 2-4 a turn against my AC 12 (much less than its 1d4 suggests, because AC 12 cuts most of the small dice), and it WAKES me if I try to rest - but a counted rest ('R' then a number) runs the full count anyway, taking the hits as they come. Spell points are the bottleneck, not hit points: 4 turns of rest bought no SP at all, so ~10+ turns of rest are needed for 1 SP. Stinking Cloud is the only weapon that can hurt it (AC 36 - a flask of oil at point blank MISSED, and so did one against the kobold at AC 24). Two casts of 11 poison would finish its remaining ~17 hp. (ask 323)
- ESCAPE LADDER in practice, measured: against Grip (AC 36, 25 hp, +10 speed, biting me for 2-4 a turn in a one-wide corridor) I could not fight it - a flask of oil at point blank missed, my whip has a 12 percent chance against AC 36, and the spell that CAN hurt it costs 2 SP while I had 1. THE SPELL POINT ECONOMY IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT, and the source explains it: player-util.c:487 player_regen_mana() computes sp_gain = msp * PY_REGEN_NORMAL + PY_REGEN_MNBASE, with PY_REGEN_NORMAL = 197 and PY_REGEN_MNBASE = 524, both in 65536ths (player-util.h:27,31), and doubled while resting. For msp = 5 that is about 0.023 SP per turn, so ONE spell point costs roughly 22 turns of rest, and a Stinking Cloud needs two. Resting beside Grip for 90 turns is not a plan. So the Phase Door scroll is not a luxury - with a 2 SP weapon and no melee that reaches, the scroll IS the weapon. (ask 327)
- PHASE DOOR ESCAPE WORKED AND COST NOTHING: 'You have 2 Scrolls of Phase Door (e)' and the cursor moved from level (44,14) to level (52,8) - 10 grids, exactly as the scroll says ('When read, it teleports you randomly 10 grids'), and the monster list then said 'You can see no monsters', so Grip was left behind with no cost and no delay that I could see. The scroll is BUG-free for this job: 1 ask to open the pack, 1 to select the scroll, 1 to read it, and a 10-grid teleport. The lesson for any character with no working melee: the Phase Door scroll, not the spellbook, is the weapon. What I still cannot do is kill Grip - 25 hp at AC 36 with 1d4 and +10 speed, and a spell I cannot pay for. (ask 333)
- GREY MOULD KILLED at range 1 with one flask (2 hp, AC 1 - a certain hit at that range, 3 experience). The mould was the one monster on this level that could actually reach and hurt me: it is MOBILE (no NEVER_MOVE flag, unlike the mushroom patches) and it does 2 x SPORE:HURT:1d4, so up to 8 damage a turn against my AC 12. Two bites of it brought me from 25 to 22. It bit me while I was trying to read a scroll, which is worth knowing: a spell or scroll takes a turn, and the turn the spell resolves on is a turn the monster also acts. (ask 348)
- THE BEST SCANNING TOOL IN THE GAME, found by accident: cast Detect Life and then press '['. The detection sets MFLAG_SHOW on every living monster within 22 rows x 40 columns (effect-handler-general.c detect_monsters), and the '[' list then shows a SECOND section headed 'You are aware of N monsters:' with the glyph, count, name, sleep state and the exact relative position of each - including monsters that are out of sight and were not in the 'You can see' list. At ask 361 that gave me: Grip 5 S 3 W, a green worm mass (asleep) 17 S 3 W, and TWO giant yellow centipedes (2 asleep) - all invisible to the eye and all on the map. This is worth more than the spell's own effect: the spell is the only thing in the game that gives a player a monster list over a 22x40 area, and the manual never says so. (ask 361)
- SPELL POINT ECONOMY MEASURED, and it is the single most important number for a druid: with msp = 5 at CL3, player_regen_mana() gives sp_gain = msp * PY_REGEN_NORMAL + PY_REGEN_MNBASE = 5*197 + 524 = 1509 in 65536ths = 0.023 spell points per turn, doubled to about 0.046 while resting. So ONE spell point costs roughly 22 turns of RESTING and 43 turns of not resting, and a Stinking Cloud needs two of them. I rested 20 turns and gained nothing at all (SP stayed 1/5, HP went to 26/26). For a class whose only good spell costs 2 SP, the spell book is nearly decorative until the character can afford to sit still for a minute of game time. (ask 363)
- GRIP KILLED at ask 367: 'Grip, Farmer Maggot's Dog, dies. Welcome to level 4.' Three flasks of oil in total against it, two of them hitting, at ranges 1 and 2. That is the whole recipe for a DL2 unique as a CL3 druid: never melee it (my whip is 1d3+1 at to-hit 19 against its AC 36 - a 12 percent chance), never rely on the spell (2 spell points that take 43 turns of rest to earn), and just throw oil from range until one lands. It gave 30 experience and took me from NXT 12 to level 4. Final state: depth 2, CL4, 26/26 HP, 1/5 SP, 24 flasks of oil, 3 Cure Light Wounds, 1 Scroll of Word of Recall, AC 12, and no down staircase found on depth 2. (ask 367)
- CL4, HP 26/33, SP 1/7, NXT 28 (so CL5 needs 28 more). Studied Fox Form at CL4: the spell list at CL4 is Detect Life (1 sp), Fox Form (2 sp), Remove Hunger (2 sp), Stinking Cloud (2 sp, 'dam 12, rad 2' now that I know it - it was 11 at CL3, so the poison scales with level as class.txt says: PLAYER_LEVEL/2 + 10). Confuse Monster is CL5 and Slow Monster CL6, so neither is available yet. Fox Form (shape.txt: combat:-3:-3:3 = -3 to-hit, -3 to-dam, +3 AC; STR[-3], BLOWS[1], MOVES[1], FREE_ACT, FEATHER) is the druid's only intrinsic escape, and I had just been chased by a +10 speed dog that I could only fight with oil. Its costs are real: -3 to my already weak whip, -3 STR, 10 experience on the first cast, and no items while shaped (no quaffing a Cure Light Wounds while a fox). (ask 370)
- Testing the Word of Recall, which no run in this repo has ever used: read in the dungeon it sets a timer (player->word_recall = randint0(20) + 15 turns, effect-handler-general.c:1141) and when it expires it takes you to town ('You feel yourself yanked upwards!', game-world.c:709-727). The timer is NOT interrupted by damage - it is a plain countdown - so it is only a safe way home when nothing is chasing you, which is exactly why c15 ESC-04 does not count it as an escape. (ask 374)
- WORD OF RECALL VERIFIED, and it is better than the manual says. Read in the dungeon: 'The air about you becomes charged...', the status line then shows 'Recall' between Light and Fed, and after the timer expires 'You feel yourself yanked upwards!' and the depth becomes 0 (town). The timer ran about 26 turns (turn 10252 to 10501) and was NOT interrupted by anything - I simply rested through it. Crucially, arriving in town HEALED ME TO FULL (28/33 -> 33/33) and gave back 2 spell points, because town has no monsters and the character regenerates there. So the scroll is not an escape (c15 ESC-04 is right - the delay is too long to survive a chase) but it IS a free full heal and a free trip to the shops when nothing is chasing you. (ask 381)
- TOWN NAVIGATION on seed 23, from the town's own map (the town fits the screen, 66x22 in one panel): the stores are at town screen row 11 col 50 (7 Black Market), row 11 col 63 (5 Alchemist), row 11 col 23 (4 Bookseller), row 12 col 28 (6 Magic), row 12 col 36 (2 Armoury), row 12 col 43 (1 General), row 12 col 55 (8 Home), row 17 col 44 (3 Weaponsmith); the down staircase is at row 4 col 32 where you arrive. The store tiles are NOT walkable - the walkable square is the one orthogonally adjacent to the digit, and the path I computed to the Black Market from the arrival point was 6 south then 10 east. (ask 382)
- BLACK MARKET (store 7) STOCK ON SEED 23, the shop the previous run never visited: Lo-Hak the Awful (Half-Troll). Wand of Stun Monster (5 charges) 1875, Staff of Curing (7 charges) 2025, Lantern of Brightness (7500 turns) 3150, 11 Robes [2,+0] 42, 3 Sets of Gauntlets [3,+0] 72, Trident of Slay Animal (1d10) (+5,+7) 4902, 10 Arrows of Wounding (1d4) (+9,+13) 309. NO Deep Descent and NO Magic Mapping. The reason is in the source: store_create_random() in store.c picks the Black Market's stock as a random object of level player->max_depth + 5 to + 20 (so level 7 to 22 for me at depth 2), and the price is 150 percent of the true value (store.c:617) - the Deep Descent's base cost is 250, so it would have been about 375 and hopeless on 26 gold anyway. The cheapest useful thing there is a robe of +2 AC for 42 gold. (ask 384)
- ALCHEMIST STOCK ON SEED 23, LATER IN THE DAY - and it answers the previous run's open question: 'Magic Mapping 65 g did not help' and 'the Alchemist did not stock one this seed'. The Alchemist RESTOCKS EVERY DAY and rolls a fresh stock from its normal list, and the shopkeeper itself changes (Mauser the Chemist / Wizzle the Chaotic / Ga-nat the Greedy / Vella the Slender). At ask 399, under Vella the Slender, the stock was: 40 Potions of Cure Light Wounds 20, Potion of Cure Serious Wounds 70, 5 Potions of Cure Critical Wounds 200, Potion of Restore Life Levels 400, 2 Potions of Berserk Strength 80, 40 Scrolls of Phase Door 15, 3 Scrolls of Magic Mapping 65, 40 Scrolls of Remove Curse 100, 40 Scrolls of Word of Recall 125, 3 Scrolls of Recharging 200, 9 Scrolls of Holy Chant 40. SO MAGIC MAPPING IS FOR SALE - three of them - for 65 gold. I could not buy it: a street urchin stole 8 of my 26 gold in town and I was down to 18. The lesson for the next run is sharp: BUY THE MAGIC MAPPING SCROLL FIRST, in the Alchemist, on whichever day it is in stock, and go back to town for it - a level of gold spent here saves 200 asks of blind exploration. The stock rolls when the game day changes (store.c store_maint is called once per daycount, and the shopkeeper shuffles on a 1-in-z_info->store_shuffle chance per day). (ask 399)

note: FOUND A DOWN STAIRCASE on depth 1 of seed 23, at ask 161 - the first deliberate discovery of one by looking, in this repo's history. It is at screen (row 16, col 40), one step south-west of where I stood, in the little corridor south of the worm room. The '>' glyph was visible on the map since ask 160 but the previous run (minimaxflash-1) walked past that square 148 asks without ever reading it with 'l'. The game names it exactly: 'You see a down staircase, 1 S, 1 W.' So the MANUAL's 'no run has ever found a down staircase by walking' is not about the game - it is about not LOOKING at the glyphs you walk past. The M whole-level map at ask 156 did NOT show this '>' either, because the square had never been seen; the 'l' description is what proved it. (ask 161)

note: Depth 2 room decoded from the game data (vendor/angband/lib/gamedata/monster.txt): yellow mushroom patch = 1 hp, NEVER_MOVE, SPORE:TERRIFY:1d4 (the dice is the FEAR DURATION not damage), exp 2; grey MOLD (different from the grey mushroom patch!) = 2 hp, 2 x SPORE:HURT:1d4, exp 3, and it is MOBILE (speed 110, no NEVER_MOVE) so it can come to me; apprentice = 15 hp, AC 9, 1d4 melee, exp 6, spells BLIND|BLINK|CONF|MISSILE at spell-freq 12, and friends-base 20/40/80% summons 1d3 person companions when it dies. So an apprentice is a bad fight for a 13 HP CL1 druid: blink + blind + confuse is exactly what killed the Mage in NOTES.md, and killing it may spawn 1-3 more mages. DECISION: do not fight the apprentice or the grey mould; take the clear south door. Both hazardous monsters are in the far corners of the room, the south door is clear, and I need experience from something safer than this. (ask 174)

note: LOOK-MODE TRICK worth keeping: in look mode the cursor SNAPS to the next 'interesting' square (monster, item, door, staircase) in the direction pressed, skipping plain floor - one press of a direction enumerates the next thing along that line. Pressing the same direction again walks the cursor further along the same line (it does not restart from me), so 'l' then a direction repeated walks the whole line. That gives exact positions without any pixel-map reading, and it costs no turns: the room west of me enumerated as ant 5W, yellow patch 6W+1S, First Spells book 9W+1N, closed door 10W; east: grey mould 4E. note: THROW MISSED the sleeping ant at distance 2 (ask 201: 'The giant black ant is targeted... The Flask of oil breaks' with NO damage line, and ask 205 confirms the ant is still 'unhurt, asleep'). Source reading (vendor/angband/src/player-attack.c): make_ranged_throw() applies the OF_EXPLODE x3 damage ONLY if test_hit() passed - a miss breaks the flask on the floor and does nothing. The hit chance is chance_of_missile_hit_base() minus distance, against the monster's AC. The ant's AC 24 (monster.txt) is brutal: hit_chance() needs to_hit >= ac*2/3 = 16 to have any chance above the flat 12% always-hit, so at range you are mostly rolling the 12%. (ask 205)

note: KEY ERROR OF MINE, worth recording so no next run repeats it: after pressing 'l' (look) the look mode STAYS ACTIVE and swallows the next command's first key. At asks 221-225 I sent 'l', then 'va\'', then 'va1' and nothing happened - the look descriptions ('You are on an open floor', 'You see a yellow mushroom patch') kept printing and no turn passed, because the keys were being read as look-mode cursor moves, not as 'throw'. The tell is that the turn counter did not move and the message line showed a LOOK description. Press '\e' to leave look mode before any other command. With look mode properly closed, 'va\'' works exactly as advertised: 'The yellow mushroom patch is targeted' / 'Your Flask of oil hits the yellow mushroom patch' / 'The yellow mushroom patch is destroyed' (2 exp, NXT 7 -> 5). The yellow patch was the reason the west corridor was lethal - adjacent to it you get TERRIFIED. (ask 229)

note: TWO OIL THROWS AT THE SMALL KOBOLD BOTH MISSED (asks 235, 236) and it hit me for 2 (HP 20/22). Its AC 24 against my throwing skill is the problem, not the damage: hit_chance() in player-attack.c needs to_hit >= ac*2/3 = 16 to have more than the flat 12% always-hit, and a throwing flask at range 1-2 lands around 30-60. LESSON: the depth-1 monsters that are worth killing with oil are the LOW-AC ones (white worm mass AC 1, grey mould AC 1, yellow patch AC 1, mouse AC 4, centipede AC 12-14). A small kobold (AC 24) and a giant black ant (AC 24) are oil targets only from 1 tile away. The giant black ant died from range 1 with one flask; the same flask at range 2 missed. (ask 237)

note: GLYPH TABLE now decoded from vendor/angband/lib/gamedata/terrain.txt (each 'graphics:<char>:<colour>' line): space=unknown grid, .=open floor, +=closed door, '=open door (u=broken), <=UP staircase, >=DOWN staircase, 1-8=stores, #=secret door or granite/permanent wall or lava, :=pile of rubble, %=MAGMA VEIN or QUARTZ VEIN (a solid wall - the colour tells them apart, a text dump cannot), *=vein with treasure. note: THE '[' COMMAND IS THE BEST ONE-ASK SCAN IN THE GAME: it prints 'You can see N monsters:' with the glyph, the COUNT, the name and the exact relative position of each - e.g. 'c 1 giant yellow centipede 2 S 0 W' (ask 245). That is a monster-list panel with the relative offset, so a player who cannot use the map can still know exactly what is around and how far. It even offers 'Press x to turn ON sort by exp'. Combined with 'l' (look) in a direction, which snaps the cursor to the next interesting square and reports 'N N, E W', I can reconstruct the local geometry without ever reading a pixel of the map. (ask 245)

note: Found and picked up an UNIDENTIFIED scroll on depth 2 (ask 273), title 'imusto que', dropped by a small kobold at 100 feet. Deep Descent has level:10 and alloc:20:1 to 100 in object.txt, so at CL2 it is exactly this: a scroll with a random title that only identifies at level 10. Reading it at CL2 is what the knowledge in NOTES.md says to do (unknown consumables at CL1-3 are worth trying; the first use pays a little experience). If it is Deep Descent it drops me 5 levels below my deepest level reached - depth 2 + 5 = depth 7. Worst plausible case is Summon Monster (cost:0, alloc:10) or Darkness or Blessing. Word of Recall is the way home if depth 7 goes badly (read in the dungeon = town, 15-34 turns). (ask 274)

note: DECISIVE TEST of the manual's 'l>g' recipe: in look mode press '>' and the cursor jumps to the nearest KNOWN down staircase (vendor/angband/src/ui-target.c, path_nearest_known with square_isdownstairs). On depth 2 at ask 284 I tried it and there is NO known down staircase anywhere in the level I have explored - so the recipe cannot help until a '>' glyph has actually been seen. That is the real reason 'no run has ever found a down staircase': not that the staircases are rare, but that the game's own jump only works on a staircase you already know about. The way to know about one is to LOOK at the glyph (the 'l' command named it for me on depth 1: 'You see a down staircase, 1 S, 1 W'), so a player who reads every glyph on every map has a chance and a player who trusts the frontier logic does not. (ask 284)

note: SOURCE ANSWER to the repo's standing question 'is the down staircase findable at all': NO SPATIAL RULE EXISTS. gen-cave.c:1583 allocates exactly ONE down staircase per level (alloc_stairs(c, FEAT_MORE, 1, 0, ...)), gen-util.c:620 places it on a square with exactly 3 adjacent walls, and cave_find_get_grid() (gen-util.c:202) picks that square by random choice over the WHOLE level (state[] holds every square in the level and the next one is drawn with randint0). So the down staircase is uniform over the level's floor squares - there is no 'it is near the up staircase' or 'it is in the biggest room' heuristic to exploit. The level is 198x66 with up to 50 rooms (dungeon_profile.txt 'classic' params:11:50:200:2), and the map window is 36x22, so a level is about five screens wide and three tall. Finding one by walking is a matter of covering thousands of squares; the previous run's 148 asks and my 140 have not come close. The reliable routes are a Deep Descent scroll or a Magic Mapping scroll, and neither was available to me. (ask 289)

note: STINKING CLOUD SOURCE READING (effect-handler-attack.c:594, effect_handler_BALL): the flags are PROJECT_THRU|PROJECT_STOP|PROJECT_GRID|PROJECT_ITEM|PROJECT_KILL and PROJECT_PLAY is NOT among them, and project() only affects the player when PROJECT_PLAY is set (project.c:519 and :996). So a druid's Stinking Cloud CANNOT hit the caster, even when the ball is centred on a monster 2 tiles away. That is a big deal for a 26 HP druid: the radius-2 poison ball is a safe weapon at point blank range. Damage = PLAYER_LEVEL/2 + 10 = 11 poison at CL3, halved with distance from the centre. (ask 310)

note: ESCAPE LADDER in practice, measured: against Grip (AC 36, 25 hp, +10 speed, biting me for 2-4 a turn in a one-wide corridor) I could not fight it - a flask of oil at point blank missed, my whip has a 12 percent chance against AC 36, and the spell that CAN hurt it costs 2 SP while I had 1. THE SPELL POINT ECONOMY IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT, and the source explains it: player-util.c:487 player_regen_mana() computes sp_gain = msp * PY_REGEN_NORMAL + PY_REGEN_MNBASE, with PY_REGEN_NORMAL = 197 and PY_REGEN_MNBASE = 524, both in 65536ths (player-util.h:27,31), and doubled while resting. For msp = 5 that is about 0.023 SP per turn, so ONE spell point costs roughly 22 turns of rest, and a Stinking Cloud needs two. Resting beside Grip for 90 turns is not a plan. So the Phase Door scroll is not a luxury - with a 2 SP weapon and no melee that reaches, the scroll IS the weapon. (ask 327)

note: GREY MOULD KILLED at range 1 with one flask (2 hp, AC 1 - a certain hit at that range, 3 experience). The mould was the one monster on this level that could actually reach and hurt me: it is MOBILE (no NEVER_MOVE flag, unlike the mushroom patches) and it does 2 x SPORE:HURT:1d4, so up to 8 damage a turn against my AC 12. Two bites of it brought me from 25 to 22. It bit me while I was trying to read a scroll, which is worth knowing: a spell or scroll takes a turn, and the turn the spell resolves on is a turn the monster also acts. (ask 348)

note: THE BEST SCANNING TOOL IN THE GAME, found by accident: cast Detect Life and then press '['. The detection sets MFLAG_SHOW on every living monster within 22 rows x 40 columns (effect-handler-general.c detect_monsters), and the '[' list then shows a SECOND section headed 'You are aware of N monsters:' with the glyph, count, name, sleep state and the exact relative position of each - including monsters that are out of sight and were not in the 'You can see' list. At ask 361 that gave me: Grip 5 S 3 W, a green worm mass (asleep) 17 S 3 W, and TWO giant yellow centipedes (2 asleep) - all invisible to the eye and all on the map. This is worth more than the spell's own effect: the spell is the only thing in the game that gives a player a monster list over a 22x40 area, and the manual never says so. (ask 361)

note: SPELL POINT ECONOMY MEASURED, and it is the single most important number for a druid: with msp = 5 at CL3, player_regen_mana() gives sp_gain = msp * PY_REGEN_NORMAL + PY_REGEN_MNBASE = 5*197 + 524 = 1509 in 65536ths = 0.023 spell points per turn, doubled to about 0.046 while resting. So ONE spell point costs roughly 22 turns of RESTING and 43 turns of not resting, and a Stinking Cloud needs two of them. I rested 20 turns and gained nothing at all (SP stayed 1/5, HP went to 26/26). For a class whose only good spell costs 2 SP, the spell book is nearly decorative until the character can afford to sit still for a minute of game time. (ask 363)

note: GRIP KILLED at ask 367: 'Grip, Farmer Maggot's Dog, dies. Welcome to level 4.' Three flasks of oil in total against it, two of them hitting, at ranges 1 and 2. That is the whole recipe for a DL2 unique as a CL3 druid: never melee it (my whip is 1d3+1 at to-hit 19 against its AC 36 - a 12 percent chance), never rely on the spell (2 spell points that take 43 turns of rest to earn), and just throw oil from range until one lands. It gave 30 experience and took me from NXT 12 to level 4. Final state: depth 2, CL4, 26/26 HP, 1/5 SP, 24 flasks of oil, 3 Cure Light Wounds, 1 Scroll of Word of Recall, AC 12, and no down staircase found on depth 2. (ask 367)

note: CL4, HP 26/33, SP 1/7, NXT 28 (so CL5 needs 28 more). Studied Fox Form at CL4: the spell list at CL4 is Detect Life (1 sp), Fox Form (2 sp), Remove Hunger (2 sp), Stinking Cloud (2 sp, 'dam 12, rad 2' now that I know it - it was 11 at CL3, so the poison scales with level as class.txt says: PLAYER_LEVEL/2 + 10). Confuse Monster is CL5 and Slow Monster CL6, so neither is available yet. Fox Form (shape.txt: combat:-3:-3:3 = -3 to-hit, -3 to-dam, +3 AC; STR[-3], BLOWS[1], MOVES[1], FREE_ACT, FEATHER) is the druid's only intrinsic escape, and I had just been chased by a +10 speed dog that I could only fight with oil. Its costs are real: -3 to my already weak whip, -3 STR, 10 experience on the first cast, and no items while shaped (no quaffing a Cure Light Wounds while a fox). (ask 370)

note: Testing the Word of Recall, which no run in this repo has ever used: read in the dungeon it sets a timer (player->word_recall = randint0(20) + 15 turns, effect-handler-general.c:1141) and when it expires it takes you to town ('You feel yourself yanked upwards!', game-world.c:709-727). The timer is NOT interrupted by damage - it is a plain countdown - so it is only a safe way home when nothing is chasing you, which is exactly why c15 ESC-04 does not count it as an escape. (ask 374)

note: WORD OF RECALL VERIFIED, and it is better than the manual says. Read in the dungeon: 'The air about you becomes charged...', the status line then shows 'Recall' between Light and Fed, and after the timer expires 'You feel yourself yanked upwards!' and the depth becomes 0 (town). The timer ran about 26 turns (turn 10252 to 10501) and was NOT interrupted by anything - I simply rested through it. Crucially, arriving in town HEALED ME TO FULL (28/33 -> 33/33) and gave back 2 spell points, because town has no monsters and the character regenerates there. So the scroll is not an escape (c15 ESC-04 is right - the delay is too long to survive a chase) but it IS a free full heal and a free trip to the shops when nothing is chasing you. (ask 381)

note: BLACK MARKET (store 7) STOCK ON SEED 23, the shop the previous run never visited: Lo-Hak the Awful (Half-Troll). Wand of Stun Monster (5 charges) 1875, Staff of Curing (7 charges) 2025, Lantern of Brightness (7500 turns) 3150, 11 Robes [2,+0] 42, 3 Sets of Gauntlets [3,+0] 72, Trident of Slay Animal (1d10) (+5,+7) 4902, 10 Arrows of Wounding (1d4) (+9,+13) 309. NO Deep Descent and NO Magic Mapping. The reason is in the source: store_create_random() in store.c picks the Black Market's stock as a random object of level player->max_depth + 5 to + 20 (so level 7 to 22 for me at depth 2), and the price is 150 percent of the true value (store.c:617) - the Deep Descent's base cost is 250, so it would have been about 375 and hopeless on 26 gold anyway. The cheapest useful thing there is a robe of +2 AC for 42 gold. (ask 384)

note: ALCHEMIST STOCK ON SEED 23, LATER IN THE DAY - and it answers the previous run's open question: 'Magic Mapping 65 g did not help' and 'the Alchemist did not stock one this seed'. The Alchemist RESTOCKS EVERY DAY and rolls a fresh stock from its normal list, and the shopkeeper itself changes (Mauser the Chemist / Wizzle the Chaotic / Ga-nat the Greedy / Vella the Slender). At ask 399, under Vella the Slender, the stock was: 40 Potions of Cure Light Wounds 20, Potion of Cure Serious Wounds 70, 5 Potions of Cure Critical Wounds 200, Potion of Restore Life Levels 400, 2 Potions of Berserk Strength 80, 40 Scrolls of Phase Door 15, 3 Scrolls of Magic Mapping 65, 40 Scrolls of Remove Curse 100, 40 Scrolls of Word of Recall 125, 3 Scrolls of Recharging 200, 9 Scrolls of Holy Chant 40. SO MAGIC MAPPING IS FOR SALE - three of them - for 65 gold. I could not buy it: a street urchin stole 8 of my 26 gold in town and I was down to 18. The lesson for the next run is sharp: BUY THE MAGIC MAPPING SCROLL FIRST, in the Alchemist, on whichever day it is in stock, and go back to town for it - a level of gold spent here saves 200 asks of blind exploration. The stock rolls when the game day changes (store.c store_maint is called once per daycount, and the shopkeeper shuffles on a 1-in-z_info->store_shuffle chance per day). (ask 399)
